spots.name: Mole Antonelliana

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: The Mole Antonelliana is a major landmark building in Turin, Italy, named after its architect, Alessandro Antonelli. A mole in Italian is a building of monumental proportions.

names.ja: モーレ・アントネリアーナ

spots.name: Museo Egizio
spots.summary: The Museo Egizio or Egyptian Museum is an archaeological museum in Turin, Italy, specializing in Egyptian archaeology and anthropology.

spots.name: Turin Cathedral
spots.summary: Turin Cathedral or Cathedral of Saint John the Baptist is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Turin, northern Italy. Dedicated to Saint John the Baptist. It is the seat of the Archbishops of Turin.

spots.name: Royal Palace of Turin
spots.summary: The Royal Palace of Turin is a historic palace of the House of Savoy in the city of Turin in Northern Italy. It was originally built in the 16th century and was later modernized by Christine Marie of France (1606–1663) in the 17th century, with designs by the Baroque architect Filippo Juvarra.

spots.name: Palazzo Carignano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Palazzo Carignano is a historical building in the centre of Turin, Italy, which houses the Museum of the Risorgimento. It was a private residence of the Princes of Carignano, after whom it is named. Its rounded façade is different from other façades of the same structure.

spots.name: Palazzo Madama, Turin

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: Palazzo Madama is a palace in Turin, Piedmont. It was the first Senate of the Kingdom of Italy, and takes its traditional name from the embellishments it received under two queens (madama) of the House of Savoy.

names.it: Palazzo Madama e Casaforte degli Acaja

spots.name: Residences of the Royal House of Savoy
spots.summary: The Residences of the Royal House of Savoy are a group of buildings in Piedmont, northern Italy. It was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Sites list in 1997.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Residences of the Royal House of Savoy

names.nl: Residenties van het Koninklijk Huis van Savoye
names.fr: Résidences de la famille royale de Savoie
names.es: Residencias de la casa real de Saboya
names.ja: サヴォイア王家の王宮群

spots.name: Sindone Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chapel of the Holy Shroud is a Baroque style Roman Catholic chapel in Turin in northern Italy, constructed to house the Shroud of Turin, a religious relic alleged to be the burial shroud of Jesus of Nazareth. It is located adjacent to the Turin Cathedral and connected to the Royal Palace of Turin.

spots.name: Piazza Castello
spots.summary: Piazza Castello is a prominent city square in Turin, Italy. It houses several city landmarks, museums, theaters and cafes.

spots.name: Villa della Regina
spots.summary: The Villa della Regina is a once semi-rural palace, now surrounded by the city of Turin, Piedmont, Italy. It is located at Strada Santa Margherita #79 in the eastern sector of the city, in the quarter of Borgo Po. It was originally built by the House of Savoy in the 17th century.

spots.name: Santuario della Consolata
spots.summary: The Basilica of Saint Mary of Consolation, or the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Consolation, is a Roman Catholic minor basilica and Marian shrine in central Turin, Piedmont, Italy.

spots.name: San Lorenzo, Turin
spots.summary: San Lorenzo, also known as the Royal Church of Saint Lawrence, is a Baroque-style church in Turin, adjacent to the Royal Palace of Turin. The present church was designed and built by Guarino Guarini during 1668–1687.

spots.name: National Museum of Cinema

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The National Museum of Cinema located in Turin, Italy, is a motion picture museum inside the Mole Antonelliana tower. It is operated by the Maria Adriana Prolo Foundation, and the core of its collection is the result of the work of the historian and collector Maria Adriana Prolo. It was housed in the Palazzo Chiablese.

names.es: Museo Nacional del Cine de Turín

spots.name: Gran Madre di Dio
spots.summary: Gran Madre di Dio is a Neoclassic-style church in Turin, Italy, dedicated to Mary, Mother of God. It is located on the western bank of the Po River, facing the Ponte Vittorio Emanuele I leading into Piazza Vittorio Veneto.

names.fr: Église Gran Madre di Dio de Turin
names.es: Iglesia de la Gran Madre di Dio
names.it: Chiesa della Gran Madre di Dio

spots.name: Piazza San Carlo
spots.summary: Piazza San Carlo, previously known as Piazza Reale, Piazza d'Armi, and Place Napoléon, is one of the main city squares in Turin, Italy. It was laid out in the 16th and 17th century and is an example of Baroque style.

spots.name: Museo dell'Automobile
spots.summary: The Museo Nazionale dell'Automobile di Torino, known as MAUTO, is an automobile museum in Turin, Italy, founded by Carlo Biscaretti di Ruffia. The museum has a collection of almost 200 cars among eighty automobile brands representing eight countries .

spots.name: Castello del Valentino

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Valentino Castle is a historic building in the northwestern Italian city of Turin. It is located in Parco del Valentino, and is the seat of the Architecture Faculty of the Polytechnic University of Turin.

spots.name: San Filippo Neri

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Filippo Neri is a late-Baroque style, Roman Catholic church located in Turin, region of Piedmont, Italy. The church is located on Via Maria Vittoria 5; the left flank of the nave faces the Turin Academy of Sciences. The church is still used for services.

spots.name: Museum of the Risorgimento

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum of the Italian Risorgimento is the first, the biggest and the most important among the 23 museums in Italy dedicated to the Risorgimento; and the only one which can be considered "national" according to a 1901 law, and due to its rich and great collections.

names.ja: リソルジメント博物館
names.zh: 意大利复兴运动国家博物馆

spots.name: Parco del Valentino
spots.summary: Parco del Valentino is a popular public park in Turin, Italy. It is located along the west bank of the Po river. It covers an area of 500,000m², which makes it Turin's second largest park . This park has been nominated “The best Italian park” after a selection among the fifteen best Italian parks.

names.ja: ヴァレンティーノ公園

spots.name: Galleria Sabauda
spots.summary: The Savoy Gallery is an art collection in the Italian city of Turin, which contains the royal art collections amassed by the House of Savoy over the centuries. It is located on Via XX Settembre, 86.

spots.name: Borgo Medioevale
spots.summary: The Borgo Medioevale is an open air museum and reconstructed medieval village and castle in Turin, Italy. It is located in the Parco del Valentino on the riverbank of the Po river.

names.it: Borgo e rocca medievale di Torino

spots.name: Palazzo Chiablese

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Chiablese is a wing of the Royal Palace of Turin, in Northwest Italy.

spots.name: Piazza Vittorio Veneto
spots.summary: Piazza Vittorio Veneto, also known as Piazza Vittorio, is a city square in Turin, Italy, which takes its name from the Battle of Vittorio Veneto in 1918. It was formerly known as Piazza Vittorio Emanuele I, after the Savoyard king Victor Emmanuel I.

spots.name: Royal Armoury of Turin
spots.summary: The Royal Armoury of Turin is one of the world's most important collections of arms and armour, formed in Turin by the Savoy family. The museum is now part of the Musei Reali di Torino, the royal site that has unified the Royal Palace, the Sabauda Gallery, the Archaeological Museum, the Royal Library and the Armoury.

spots.name: Fetta di Polenta

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casa Scaccabarozzi, commonly known as Fetta di Polenta, is a historic building located in the Vanchiglia neighborhood of the northern Italian city of Turin. It is famous for its unusual and very thin trapezoidal plan and for being only 54 centimetres (1.77 ft) at its narrowest.

spots.name: Santa Cristina, Turin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Cristina is a Baroque style, Roman Catholic church located in Turin, region of Piedmont, Italy. It mirrors the adjacent church of San Carlo and faces the Piazza San Carlo.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Carlo Borromeo or San Carlo is a Baroque style, Roman Catholic church located in Turin, region of Piedmont, Italy. It mirrors the adjacent church of Santa Cristina and faces the Piazza San Carlo.

spots.name: Museo Civico d'Arte Antica

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Museo Civico d'Arte Antica is an art museum located in the Palazzo Madama in Turin, Italy. It has a renowned collection of paintings from the medieval, Renaissance and Baroque periods. It reopened in 2006 after several years of restorations.

names.nl: Turin City Museum of Ancient Art

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Basilica of Our Lady Help of Christians
spots.summary: The Basilica of Our Lady Help of Christians is a Pontifical church and Marian shrine in Turin, Italy. The building was originally part of the safehouse for poor boys cared for by Don Bosco; it now contains the remains of Bosco.

spots.name: Teatro Regio
spots.summary: The Teatro Regio is a prominent opera house and opera company in Turin, Piedmont, Italy. Its season runs from October to June with the presentation of eight or nine operas given from five to twelve performances of each.

spots.name: Pinacoteca Giovanni e Marella Agnelli

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Pinacoteca Giovanni e Marella Agnelli or Pinacoteca Agnelli is an art gallery in Turin, Italy. It opened in 2002 on the top floor of the Lingotto complex, the headquarters of the Italian auto giant Fiat S.p.A. founded in 1899 by Giovanni Agnelli.

spots.name: Monument to Emanuele Filiberto
spots.summary: The Equestrian monument of Emmanuel Philibert, commonly known as Caval ëd bronz, rises in the center of Piazza San Carlo in central Turin, in the Piedmont region of Italy.

spots.name: Basilica of Corpus Domini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Corpus Domini is a Roman Catholic church in Turin, Italy, built to celebrate the "Miracle of the Eucharist" which, according to various sources, occurred in 1453 during the war between the Duchy of Savoy and France.

spots.name: Porta Palatina
spots.summary: The Palatine Gate is a Roman Age city gate located in Turin, Italy. The gate provided access through the city walls of Julia Augusta Taurinorum from the North side and, as a result, it constituted the Porta Principalis Dextra of the old town.

spots.name: Museum of Oriental Art

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of Oriental Art is a museum located in a 17th-century palazzo in the city of Turin, Italy.

spots.name: Palazzo Barolo

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Baroque bling palace, visit by guided tour. Its last private owner Carlo Tancredi Falletti di Barolo served Napoleon then worked tirelessly for relief of the poor; his palace then became an opera house.

spots.name: Royal Library of Turin

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Royal Library of Turin is a library located within the ground floor of the Royal Palace of Turin, itself a World Heritage Site in Turin, Italy.

spots.name: Piazza Statuto
spots.summary: Piazza Statuto is a city square in Turin, Italy.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Grattacielo Intesa Sanpaolo in Turin, Italy is a skyscraper as well as the headquarters for the banking group Intesa Sanpaolo.

spots.name: Santa Maria al Monte dei Cappuccini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Santa Maria al Monte dei Cappuccini is a late-Renaissance-style church on a hill overlooking the River Po just south of the bridge of Piazza Vittorio Veneto in Turin, Italy. It was built for the Capuchin Order; construction began in 1583 and was completed in 1656.

spots.name: Teatro Carignano
spots.summary: The Teatro Carignano is a theatre in Turin and one of the oldest and most important theatres in Italy. Designed by Benedetto Alfieri, it is located opposite the Palazzo Carignano.

spots.summary: The cappella dei Mercanti, Negozianti e Banchieri, better known as cappella dei Mercanti, is a Catholic chapel in the historic city center of Turin, Italy.

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Turin Civic Gallery of Modern and Contemporary Art is an art gallery in Turin, Italy, founded in 1891-1895 and located in 31 via Magenta. With the MAO, Palazzo Madama e Casaforte degli Acaja, the Borgo and the Rocca medioevali, it forms part of the Fondazione Torino Musei.

spots.name: State Archives of Turin
spots.summary: The State Archives of Turin is a public archival institution located in Turin, Italy. It preserves historical records relating to the governmental and administrative institutions that operated in Piedmont and in the territories ruled by the House of Savoy.

spots.name: Torino Esposizioni
spots.summary: Torino Esposizioni is an exhibition hall and convention centre in Turin, Italy which was primarily completed in 1948, designed by Pier Luigi Nervi.

spots.name: Galleria d'Italia

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Galleria d'Italia is a museum chain to show off the art owned by Intesa Sanpaolo bank, the modern nobility. The Turin branch, opened in 2022, is in the Palazzo Turinetti di Pertengo and mostly displays photography. Their others are in Milan, Naples and Vicenza.

spots.name: CAMERA – Italian Centre for Photography
spots.summary: Impressive quality photography, with 3 or 4 exhibitions a year.

spots.name: Museo Regionale di Scienze Naturali
spots.summary: Trad natural history display of rocks and stuffed animals in a former hospital.

spots.name: Piano35
spots.summary: This teeters atop a skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, occupied by Intesa Sanpaolo Bank. High scores for food and service, and you're paying for the rooftop view.

spots.name: Mare Nostrum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Excellent southern Italian and Sicilian seafood fish dishes. The starter is a must, just one entry on the menu, but you receive six small dishes of the day.

spots.name: Birrificio Torino
spots.summary: Brewpub restaurant with six beers brewed on premises. Good menu with recommended matched beers. More restaurant than pub, it can be very busy.

spots.name: Caffe al Bicerin

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: Home of the classic Torinese drink, the Bicerin, a mix of coffee, hot chocolate and cream. But pricey and long queues.

spots.name: Focacceria Lagrange
spots.summary: Nice place to eat light and crispy focaccia. Fast service. Mostly takeaway but they have a few tables inside and out.

spots.name: Lobelix

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat

spots.summary: This bar serves a nightly aperitivo - your drink buys access to the food, which runs out towards 21:00.

spots.name: Birichin
spots.summary: Gourmet restaurant with wide selection of Italian fare and huge wine selection, mostly good reviews.

spots.name: Caffe Rossini

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Calls itself a restaurant, but it's really a café and late-night pub with music and a young crowd.

spots.name: Da Mauro
spots.summary: Good reviews for their home cooking. Great value for money, come early or you won't get in.

spots.name: Lab Vittorio

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat

spots.summary: Small lively bar with good cocktails and tapas. They have another bar at Via Mazzini 5.

spots.name: Fratelli La Cozza
spots.summary: Pizzeria and seafood. Try for a balcony seat for views down the boulevard.

spots.name: Gofreria Piemontèisa

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Gofri are waffles Piedmont style, thin with sweet or savoury fillings.

spots.name: Mezzaluna

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Friendly staff serving vegan versions of Italian and other dishes.

spots.name: Piola Cianci
spots.summary: Popular place for fast inexpensive antipasti and main meals.

spots.name: Pizzeria Due Torri
spots.summary: Good pizza and pasta dishes. Friendly efficient staff.

spots.name: Trattoria San Domenico
spots.summary: Traditional Italian food, with Sardinian specialities.
